subject: Qualification deep-dive: benchmark cookbook & SLO parameters
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Qualification deep-dive: benchmark cookbook & SLO parameters

Alex — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick written recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so we have a single reference for the benchmark work and SLO alignment.

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Business objective: pilot Redwood to power real-time product recommendations in checkout flows (low-latency scoring + streaming product card generation).
- Latency targets (customer asks): p95 end-to-end generation <= 250ms for synchronous scoring paths; p99 <= 600ms when under steady load. For streaming product-card assembly, time-to-first-token (TTFT) target <= 80ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state steady throughput target ~200 QPS; sustained bursts up to 600 QPS. Expected concurrency of 40–60 simultaneous sessions for the busiest endpoints.
- Model constraints: preference for 7B/13B open models with 4-bit quantization if accuracy holds; team will confirm acceptable model families.
- Data & reproducibility: test corpus should mirror production prompts (sanitized). You asked for explicit measurement definitions so you can compare runs across teams — we'll provide a concise cookbook.

What I’m attaching now: acme_benchmark_prompt_set_v1.json (sanitized sample prompts) and redwood_harness_instructions_v2.md (runbook + measurement spec). These contain: canonical prompt bundles, expected token accounting rules, and basic harness commands we use for reproducible runs.

Key measurement definitions (high-level — full detail in the attached runbook):
- Latency (p95/p99): measured server-side from request-received to last-byte-delivered; for streaming, TTFT is measured to first-byte-delivered.
- Throughput: measured as sustained QPS at steady-state (30s stable window) — exclude warmup/ramp.
- Concurrency semantics: concurrent sessions = independent request streams with isolated KV caches. We’ll define cache-warmup policy in the harness.
- Reproducibility: fixed seed where applicable, explicit model version tag, hardware snapshot (GPU type, driver, CUDA/cuDNN), runtime container image.

Proposed next steps:
1) You to confirm whether the provided prompt set is representative and any additions you want (security-sensitive prompts redacted).
2) Marissa (CC’d) to run an initial baseline on Redwood test harness next week — we propose Tue/Wed window (we’ll confirm timezone).
3) If procurement requires, loop in procurement@acme-retail.com and I’ll share a short SOW/statement of work template.

If that aligns, Marissa will schedule the benchmark run and send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

—
Priyom Das

Alex — great questions. Pasted below are the precise specs we use in the harness (short form). The full detail is in redwood_harness_instructions_v2.md attached. Marissa / Neha, please chime if I miss anything.

Bench harness: quick specs
- Model execution modes supported: FP16 (full precision) and 4-bit quantized (q4_k_mixed). Harness will run both variants and annotate results.
- Hardware baseline for reproducibility: A100 80GB (PCIe or SXM) with NVIDIA driver 525.x, CUDA 12.x. Please record GPU utilization and temperature snapshots.
- Latency definitions:
  * TTFT (streaming): measured at the server NGINX proxy layer from request arrival to first byte sent downstream.
  * Total generation latency (sync): measured from request-received to last-byte-sent at the same proxy. Both measured per-request and aggregated to p50/p95/p99.
- Throughput measurement: steady-state QPS computed over a sliding 30s window after a 60s warmup. We record both offered load and accepted completions so we can show saturation points.
- Concurrency semantics: runs will include scenarios with isolated KV caches per session and scenarios with shared, warmed cache to reflect production.
- Batch sizing: harness will sweep batch sizes (1, 2, 4, 8) and record latency/throughput trade-offs.
- Random seeds & determinism: when models support deterministic sampling, we set seeds and log RNG state. Otherwise, we record sampling temperature and note nondeterminism in the run metadata.

Repro checklist (what we attach to every run):
- model_name | model_tag
- quantization_profile
- docker image tag (we’ll attach a small manifest)
- GPU snapshot (type/driver/kernel)
- harness commit SHA + command line invocation
- prompt set file and any post-processing script

Marissa — can you attach the Dockerfile/runtime manifest (minimal) and the harness command snippet? Neha — please flag any security/compliance notes for the procurement packet.

Proposed bench window: Wed 2027-04-28, 09:00–12:00 PDT (we can do a follow-up in the afternoon if the initial runs saturate). If that works for your infra team Alex, I’ll lock it in and send invites.

—
Priyom
